Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there visible evidence that the paper has been moved toward or into the cup, even if it is not yet stuffed inside?
node.criteria: Pass if visible evidence shows progress toward placing the paper into the cup, but the paper is not visibly stuffed inside it. Fail if there is no visible progress toward the requested placement, or if the paper is visibly stuffed inside the cup. Unknown if the image does not provide enough evidence to determine progress.
node.binding: Progress counts only when it advances the requested act of stuffing the paper into the cup; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a hand holding the paper near the cup, but the paper is not visibly being moved toward or into the cup; there is no visible progress toward stuffing it.

fulfillment: The node’s decision logic appears sound: the edited image shows a hand holding a paper-like object outside the cup, with no visible movement toward or placement in it, supporting “no” under the rubric. Preserve the distinction between complete fulfillment and partial progress, and do not treat the reference label as atomic ground truth. However, the trace’s claim that the object is near the cup is not grounded in the supplied edited image: no cup is visible, and the object’s identity as the requested paper is uncertain. Tighten the binding/evidence criteria to require identifying the relevant paper and cup in the edited image before judging placement or progress; when either cannot be identified, return unknown rather than infer absence from an unverified comparison. Keep this visual-evidence issue separate from transport or execution failures: the node ran validly, but its stated evidence overclaims what the image shows.
